A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sparsing Law study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–L support a reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: V2 reports original model-training, sparsity-measurement, downstream-evaluation, and inference-speed experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results, including the 0.1B–1.2B model studies and the 2.4B model's sparsity and acceleration results.

M1.justification: The CETT-PPL-p% metric, model architecture, and binary-search procedure are unchanged. Algorithm 1 is relocated and its validation-set variable changes from ValidSet to VS without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training corpora, downstream benchmarks, four domains for activation-pattern analysis, and C4 acceleration-test prompts. Appendices H and K retain the same coverage, including the more complex benchmarks.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Straightforward ReLU, Top-k, and FAT-epsilon against CETT, along with the retained MoE and acceleration comparisons. CATS and TEAL are newly discussed in Section 2.2 but are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Model scales, training and decay policies, benchmark shot counts, metrics, and PPL tolerances remain unchanged. Appendix L retains the acceleration protocol using 100 prompts with five prefix tokens.

E4.justification: Both retain the PPL-tolerance analysis, nine-width/depth study, model-scale and activation-pattern analyses, MoE comparison, and supplementary training-loss analyses. No analytical question or supporting experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Curve-fitting and checkpoint-averaging practices remain unchanged, including the last-five-checkpoint strategy in Appendix E. There is no added seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1, 2, and 4–6 and the plotted results are unchanged. Both retain the 2.4B model's 6.48% limiting activation ratio and decoding speeds of 41.79 versus 10.23 tokens per second.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the sparsity definitions, fitted functional forms, and neuron-specialization assumptions and derivation are retained. The algorithm's variable rename introduces no mathematical change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about CETT-PPL-1%, sparsity scaling, ReLU, width-depth ratios, scale insensitivity, and the 2.4B demonstration.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 newly distinguishes the paper's activation-output sparsity focus from TEAL's input sparsity and explicitly leaves quantitative input-sparsity studies to future work. Existing result interpretations and Appendix A limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds an abstract statement directing readers to the SparsingLaw repository for code and checkpoints; v2 lacks this access statement. This adds reproducibility information, although repository contents and availability cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: V3 adds CATS (Lee et al., 2024) and TEAL (Liu et al., 2024a), discussing their relationship to Top-k and the paper's sparsity focus. It removes Dai et al. (2022), while retaining the broader research positioning and novelty claim.

P1.justification: V3 adds three coauthors, a Huawei affiliation, acknowledgments, and publication information, alongside localized prose additions and edits. The scientific narrative and section and appendix ordering remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 moves from a standalone page in v2 to a single-column display beside Appendix F's explanation in v3. Figure 11 moves between columns on page 8, and surrounding text reflows; figure contents and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 supplies a stated code/checkpoint access route, adds relevant research context and an explicit scope boundary, and places Algorithm 1 beside its explanation. These provide modest documentation and accessibility gains while the empirical evidence, mathematical arguments, and existing limitations remain unchanged.
